Subject: Renewal kickoff: EU as sovereign primary + APAC warm standby?

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the heads-up that our renewal window is coming up. As we discussed on the last call, ZenWell is exploring making the EU footprint our sovereign primary region (for PHI and local processing) and adding an APAC warm-standby for burst and DR. We want to capture this in the upcoming contract and understand the implications for: term length, committed capacity (we expect a 30-40% growth over next 12 months), add-on pricing for warm standby, and SLAs for cross-region failover.

Attached is our Q1 usage snapshot to give you context: ZenWell_current_usage_Q1-2027.csv (attachment).

Can you propose a path that preserves data residency in EU while enabling an APAC pilot for October? Also, any minimum lead times for deployment or special compliance artifacts we should prepare?

Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the usage file, that helps. Looping in Marissa (pricing/renewals) and Sean (solutions/ops) to propose an actionable plan. High level — we can support EU-first data residency and configure APAC as a warm standby with controlled replication and traffic steering for failover. A couple of clarifying points before we draft a formal MAP:

- Confirm target term (12 vs 24 months) and whether you want committed reserved capacity in EU only, or reserved capacity in EU + baseline standby in APAC.
- Expected steady-state qps and peak 95th percentile for July–Dec 2027 (the Q1 file is great; if you can send recent 90/95 p95 that helps with kernel selection and pooling).
- Compliance artifacts we typically surface: SOC2 snapshot, infrastructure topology showing EU-only processing, and a statement of encryption in transit/at rest. I will ask Security for a package.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa prepares two pricing options (EU-reserved + APAC standby vs EU-reserved + on-demand APAC) with delta pricing and SLO impact.
2) Sean drafts a deployment timeline for an APAC warm-standby pilot (6–8 week window) and a cross-region failover runbook.
3) We share a draft MAP and contract redlines for your procurement team.

Sending a short MAP draft as an attachment (draft-MAP-zenwell-2027.pdf) for discussion; we'll iterate it if you confirm term and baseline capacity.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Renewal kickoff: capacity/pricing options

Hi team — following up with concrete capacity and pricing sketches based on ZenWell's Q1 and expected 35% growth. Quick summary (high-level):

Option A — EU-reserved primary + APAC on-demand standby
- EU committed GPUs: Equivalent of 8 A100-class units (target steady state).
- APAC standby: no reserved capacity, on-demand burst with 2x cold w/ warm cache (slower failover).
- Pricing delta vs current: ~+22% for EU capacity uplift.
- SLA impact: failover latency for cold APAC bursts ~+300–500 ms additional cold-start penalty; warm-cache not guaranteed.

Option B — EU-reserved primary + APAC warm-standby (recommended)
- EU committed GPUs: 7 A100-class units (right-sized with autoscale).
- APAC warm-standby: reserved minimal pool equal to 2 A100-class capacity maintained in warm mode (KV cache pre-warmed nightly), can be brought to full capacity in ~20–30 minutes with staged autoscale.
- Pricing delta vs Option A: ~+9% for the warm-standby reservation but reduces failover deficits and improves cold-start by ~70%.
- SLA impact: cross-region failover covered by our runbook; targeted end-to-end failover restore within 30 minutes for warm-standby.

I attached a quick capacity estimate workbook (capacity-estimate-zenwell.xlsx) with month-by-month cost delta and token unit economics. Key callouts:
- If you sign a 24-month term with a 10% commit uplift, we can offer a further 6% commercial credit.
- We can model a canary failover during Q4 pilot to validate runbook before full cutover.

Next steps: Jonas — do you want me to convert Option B into a draft SOW we can attach to the renewal? Marcus / Elena — any target throughput p95 numbers you can share for August and November to finalize sizing?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Pricing, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — Option B looks closest to what procurement will sign up for, assuming we get commitments on data residency and a few compliance items. A few items to confirm before procurement signs:

1) Data residency proof: can you provide an architecture diagram and an attestation that all inference (model execution) for EU-designated workloads remains in the EU cluster (no cross-region inference by default)?
2) SOC2 evidence: current SOC2 type II report or security package we can attach to the contract.
3) Contract mechanics: please send a redline-ready contract link (DocuSign or shared drive). We prefer a 24-month term with a 10% uplift commitment if you can lock in that commercial credit.

I uploaded our SOW notes and internal procurement checklist (zenwell_sow_notes.pdf) for your reference.
